name: Low Porosity Hair
description: Hair with low porosity has a tightly sealed cuticle, making it difficult for water and products to penetrate. This type of hair can be dense and resistant to changes in texture.
hair_texture: Thick, dense, and may appear frizzy or wavy
characteristics: May take longer to absorb products
common_problems: Difficult to style and maintain texture
Susceptible to buildup from product residue
recommended_ingredients: Hydrating agents like glycerin, panthenol, and hyaluronic acid
Lightweight oils such as argan or jojoba oil for moisture locking
ingredients_to_avoid: Heavy creams and waxes that can weigh down hair
washing_frequency: Every 2-3 days or as needed, being cautious not to overwash
oil_recommendation: Use light oils that do not leave a residue, applied after washing

night_routine.action: Apply lightweight oil or serum to seal in moisture
night_routine.purpose: Lock in hydration and protect overnight

weekly_care: Deep condition with a rich mask once a week
deep_conditioning_frequency: Once a week for best results
heat_styling_recommendation: Use heat protectants and limit styling tools to prevent damage
foods_for_healthy_hair: Protein-rich foods like eggs, lean meats, and fish
Fruits and vegetables rich in vitamins and minerals
common_mistakes: Overwashing the hair, which can strip natural oils
Using too many heavy products that can weigh down hair
dont: Do not use high-heat styling tools frequently
Do not skip deep conditioning sessions

seasonal_care.summer: Use lighter, oil-free products and avoid direct sunlight to prevent overheating of the scalp.
seasonal_care.winter: Increase hydration with richer products to combat dryness from cold weather.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Stay extra hydrated by drinking water and using hydrating shampoos and conditioners more frequently.

expert_tips: Regular trims can help maintain the health of low porosity hair.
Experiment with different products to find what works best for your specific hair texture.
